text:
Our remedies oft in ourselves do lie,
Which we ascribe to heaven: the fated sky
Gives us free scope; only doth backward pull
Our slow designs when we ourselves are dull.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: You blame the stars, but mostly you are the thing holding you back.

text:
Love all, trust a few,
Do wrong to none. Be able for thine enemy
Rather in power than use; and keep thy friend
Under thy own life’s key. Be check’d for silence,
But never tax’d for speech.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Love widely, trust slowly, hurt no one, and keep your friends close. Say less than you could.

text:
Impossible be strange attempts to those
That weigh their pains in sense, and do suppose
What hath been cannot be.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Impossible things only look that way to people who count the cost of trying.

text:
Oft expectation fails, and most oft there
Where most it promises; and oft it hits
Where hope is coldest, and despair most fits.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: Expected wins often fail, and the long shots land where hope was lowest. Keep going.

text:
Good alone
Is good without a name; vileness is so:
The property by what it is should go,
Not by the title. She is young, wise, fair;
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 2 Scene 3
plain: A thing is what it is, not what it is called. Judge by the substance, not the title.

text: Moderate lamentation is the right of the dead; excessive grief the enemy to the living.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Grieve in measure. Too much grief hurts the living more than it honors the dead.

text:
’Tis not the many oaths that makes the truth,
But the plain single vow that is vow’d true.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 2
plain: One vow kept beats a thousand oaths sworn.

text: Now, God delay our rebellion! As we are ourselves, what things are we!
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 3
plain: Admit it: we are our own worst enemy, and we know it.

text:
I have felt so many quirks of joy and grief
That the first face of neither on the start
Can woman me unto ’t.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 3 Scene 2
plain: Real hardship has taught her not to be thrown by the first look of joy or grief.

text: The web of our life is of a mingled yarn, good and ill together; our virtues would be proud if our faults whipped them not; and our crimes would despair if they were not cherish’d by our virtues.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 3
plain: Life is good and bad woven together. Wins keep you humble, flaws keep you from despair.

text:
Let’s take the instant by the forward top;
For we are old, and on our quick’st decrees
Th’inaudible and noiseless foot of time
Steals ere we can effect them.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 5 Scene 3
plain: Grab the moment now. Time moves silently and steals the thing you meant to do.

text:
Our rash faults
Make trivial price of serious things we have,
Not knowing them until we know their grave.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 5 Scene 3
plain: We treat what we have as cheap until it is gone.

text:
All’s well that ends well; still the fine’s the crown.
Whate’er the course, the end is the renown.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 4
plain: If it ends well, the rough road was worth it. The finish is what counts.

text:
But with the word the time will bring on summer,
When briers shall have leaves as well as thorns,
And be as sweet as sharp.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 4
plain: Be patient. Summer is coming, and the thorns will have leaves too.

text:
Simply the thing I am
Shall make me live.
location: All's Well That Ends Well, Act 4 Scene 3
plain: Just being what I am is enough to keep me going.

text: There’s beggary in the love that can be reckoned.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Love you can put a number on is not much of a love.

text:
Let Rome in Tiber melt, and the wide arch
Of the ranged empire fall! Here is my space.
Kingdoms are clay. Our dungy earth alike
Feeds beast as man.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1 Scene 1
plain: Empires are dust. We all end up the same earth, so what you build with people matters more.

text: Things that are past are done with me. ’Tis thus:
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: The past is finished with me. I deal with what is in front of me.

text:
Who tells me true, though in his tale lie death,
I hear him as he flattered.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Tell me the truth even if it hurts. I would rather hear it than be flattered.

text:
O, then we bring forth weeds
When our quick minds lie still, and our ills told us
Is as our earing. Fare thee well awhile.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Without hard truths, the mind goes to seed. Criticism is the plowing that keeps it growing.

text: The nature of bad news infects the teller.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1 Scene 2
plain: Bringing bad news earns you the blame. People punish the messenger.

text: In time we hate that which we often fear.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1 Scene 3
plain: We come to hate what we keep fearing.

text:
Whiles we are suitors to their throne, decays
The thing we sue for.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: Waiting and begging for a thing can make it wither before it arrives.

text:
We, ignorant of ourselves,
Beg often our own harms, which the wise powers
Deny us for our good; so find we profit
By losing of our prayers.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: We often pray for what would hurt us. Some unanswered prayers were a favor.

text:
My salad days,
When I was green in judgment, cold in blood,
To say as I said then.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1 Scene 5
plain: Looking back on the fool you were at twenty. You were green and sure of yourself.

text:
Age cannot wither her, nor custom stale
Her infinite variety. Other women cloy
The appetites they feed, but she makes hungry
Where most she satisfies.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 2 Scene 2
plain: Real pull never fades. Other things feed the hunger, she keeps you hungry.

text:
Caesar gets money where
He loses hearts.
location: Antony and Cleopatra, Act 2 Scene 1
plain: Some people win cash and lose loyalty. The trade is not worth it.
